addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- codebase-pattern-finder: codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- thoughts-analyzer: The research equivalent of codebase-analyzer. Use this subagent_type when wanting to deep dive on a research topic. Not commonly needed otherwise. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- thoughts-locator: Discovers relevant documents in thoughts/ directory (We use this for all sorts of metadata storage!). This is really only relevant/needed when you're in a reseaching mood and need to figure out if we have random thoughts written down that are relevant to your current research task. Based on the name, I imagine you can guess this is the `thoughts` equivilent of `codebase-locator` (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

POSITION counts by state and depth · FRONTIER ready but not yet EXPLAINED
BLOCKING below EXPLAINED and gating others, ranked · GAPS never swept
NEXT one concept, why, what done looks like

# PHASE 1 — CONCEPTS: build the map

Invoked by `/tutor concepts <dir>`. Produces the question bank. Nothing else in
the system works until this exists, because every later phase draws from it.

## Why this phase exists

He cannot report a gap he has no name for. He designed a bounded worker pool with
token-based admission control and did not know those words — so he could not
search for it, say it in an interview, or recognise it in someone else's code.
**Unnamed knowledge feels like no knowledge.** This phase gives every technique
already present in his own code its industry name.

It also solves unknown-unknowns without guessing: the code enumerates the
concepts. Anything in the file he cannot name is a gap. Coverage is guaranteed by
the source, not by the agent's imagination.

## Procedure

1. Read EVERY source file in `<dir>`. Not a sample. Not the docstrings.
2. Extract every distinct concept actually present:
   - `language`  — syntax and semantics (`yield`, `nonlocal`, `with`, decorators,
     truthiness, mutable default args, closures, `__name__`)
   - `stdlib`    — APIs used (`pathlib`, `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode`, `codecs`,
     `sqlite3`, `argparse`, `re`)
   - `pattern`   — design (generator pipeline, correlation ID, checkpointing,
     idempotency, bounded worker pool, admission control, reconciliation)
   - `failure`   — how errors are handled (fail-safe default, retry, partial
     failure accounting, poison-record isolation)
   - `api`       — provider mechanics (batch endpoints, structured outputs,
     token budgets, rate limits)
   - `arch`      — how the whole thing is shaped (orchestrator, ledger, staging)
3. For each, record: `slug`, industry `name`, one-line `definition`, `category`,
   `depth` 1-5, and `file:line` where it lives IN HIS CODE with a short `snippet`.
4. `depth`: 1 = primitive a beginner meets first · 3 = intermediate · 5 = system
   architecture. Depth drives sweep order — shallow first, so coverage is broad.
5. Insert into `concepts` with `state='UNKNOWN'`, `swept_in=NULL`. Grade NOTHING
   here. This phase names; it does not judge.
6. Set `requires` only where genuinely true (`generator` requires `function-def`).
   A guessed prerequisite is worse than none.
7. Report: total concepts, count per category, count per depth. That number is
   the visible edge of the territory — say it out loud. It is finite and it is
   smaller than he fears.

## Rules

- Every concept must point at real code in `<dir>`. No concept he does not
  already own. This is an inventory, not a syllabus.
- Use the name a job description would use, not a teaching name.
- Never teach in this phase. Never grade. Name and locate only.
- Regenerate only when the code changes. Never re-derive per session — a list
  that shifts each time makes coverage meaningless.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Prompt-runner pipeline (NOT translation).
4	
5	For every record in each input JSON file, send its `prompt` field to the OpenAI
6	Batch API, take back whatever the model writes, and produce an output record that
7	is the ORIGINAL record with `prompt` REPLACED IN PLACE by `response`. Every other
8	key (ids, names, ...) is preserved exactly and untouched.
9	
10	Pipeline pieces (mirror the translation pipeline):
11	  (1) LOADER    - stream each JSON array record-by-record, take first --limit per file
12	  (2) BUILDER   - one JSONL request per record (custom_id = <fileslug>__<index>)
13	  (3) SUBMIT    - upload + create batch on OpenAI
14	  (4) POLL      - wait for completion
15	  (5) DOWNLOAD  - fetch results.jsonl
16	  (6) MERGER    - drop `prompt`, insert `response` in its place, keep all other keys
17	  (7) OUTPUT    - write <name>_responses.json (one record per line)
18	
19	Usage:
20	    python run_prompts.py --dry-run                 # build JSONL only, no API call
21	    python run_prompts.py --submit --wait           # first 50 from each file (default)
22	    python run_prompts.py --limit 50 --submit --wait
23	    python run_prompts.py --model gpt-4.1-nano --submit --wait
24	    python run_prompts.py --files exec/pays_ville_exec.json --limit 10 --submit --wait
25	"""
26	
27	import argparse
28	import codecs
29	import json
30	import os
31	import re
32	import time
33	import uuid
34	from datetime import datetime
35	from pathlib import Path
36	
37	import openai
38	
39	BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
40	# OpenAI key lives in the soufiane_prompts folder .env.
41	ENV_PATH = BASE_DIR.parent / '.env'
42	
43	
44	def load_dotenv():
45	    """Load settings from soufiane_prompts/.env. Real env wins."""
46	    if not ENV_PATH.exists():
47	        return
48	    for line in ENV_PATH.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines():
49	        line = line.strip()
50	        if not line or line.startswith('#') or '=' not in line:
51	            continue
52	        key, value = line.split('=', 1)
53	        os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'"))
54	
55	
56	# .env must be loaded BEFORE the config block below, otherwise PROMPT_* settings
57	# in the .env are silently ignored (they would be read before the file is parsed).
58	load_dotenv()
59	
60	# ---- config --------------------------------------------------------------
61	DEFAULT_MODEL = os.getenv('PROMPT_MODEL', 'gpt-4.1-nano')  # nano by default here
62	TEMPERATURE = float(os.getenv('PROMPT_TEMPERATURE', '0.0'))
63	TOP_P = float(os.getenv('PROMPT_TOP_P', '1.0'))
64	SEED = int(os.getenv('PROMPT_SEED', '42'))
65	MAX_TOKENS = int(os.getenv('PROMPT_MAX_TOKENS', '3000'))
66	
67	# Léger rappel de rôle. Le vrai contenu (rôle + tâche) vit déjà dans le user
68	# prompt de chaque fichier ; ce system prompt sert uniquement à s'assurer que
69	# le modèle respecte scrupuleusement ces consignes.
70	SYSTEM_PROMPT = os.getenv('PROMPT_SYSTEM', (
71	    "Tu es un assistant rigoureux. Suis EXACTEMENT et intégralement les "
72	    "instructions données dans le message de l'utilisateur.\n"
73	    "RÈGLES ABSOLUES :\n"
74	    "1. Réponds UNIQUEMENT avec un objet JSON valide — aucun texte avant ou "
75	    "après, pas de balises markdown (```), pas de commentaires.\n"
76	    "2. Respecte EXACTEMENT la structure décrite dans la section « FORMAT DE "
77	    "RÉPONSE ATTENDU » du message : mêmes noms de clés, même imbrication, même "
78	    "nombre de champs. N'ajoute AUCUNE clé, n'en supprime aucune, n'invente "
79	    "aucune question ni réponse supplémentaire.\n"
80	    "3. Recopie les questions fournies MOT POUR MOT (lignes ❖ ou listes "
81	    "« Catégorie E / F »), dans l'ordre. Ne les reformule JAMAIS, n'en invente "
82	    "aucune, ne les adapte pas à la ville.\n"
83	    "4. Respecte IMPÉRATIVEMENT le nombre de mots imposé. « 80-120 mots » "
84	    "signifie AU MINIMUM 80 mots : compte-les et développe si nécessaire. "
85	    "Aucun champ ne doit être vide.\n"
86	    "5. N'ajoute aucun titre, aucune explication et aucun texte hors de ce qui "
87	    "est demandé."
88	))
89	
90	# The five input files.
91	DEFAULT_FILES = [
92	    'exec/pays_ville_exec.json',
93	    'exec/prompts_exec_profile_ville.json',
94	    'marche/prompts_type1_pays_marche.json',
95	    'marche/prompts_type2_pays_ville_marche.json',
96	    'marche/prompts_type3_pays_ville_presentation.json',
97	]

99	# ---- Structured Outputs: one strict JSON schema per input file -----------
100	# Each file's prompts demand a specific response structure (section "FORMAT DE
101	# RÉPONSE ATTENDU"). OpenAI's strict json_schema mode FORCES the model to emit
102	# exactly that structure — no malformed JSON, no missing/extra keys possible.
103	
104	def _qa_group():
105	    """questions_e / questions_f block: exactly question_1..5 + reponse_1..5."""
106	    props, req = {}, []
107	    for i in range(1, 6):
108	        props[f'question_{i}'] = {'type': 'string'}
109	        props[f'reponse_{i}'] = {'type': 'string'}
110	        req += [f'question_{i}', f'reponse_{i}']
111	    return {'type': 'object', 'properties': props, 'required': req,
112	            'additionalProperties': False}
113	
114	_SCHEMA_BLOC_ONLY = {
115	    'type': 'object',
116	    'properties': {'bloc_principal': {'type': 'string'}},
117	    'required': ['bloc_principal'],
118	    'additionalProperties': False,
119	}
120	_SCHEMA_FLAT_QA = {
121	    'type': 'object',
122	    'properties': {'bloc_principal': {'type': 'string'},
123	                   'questions_e': _qa_group(), 'questions_f': _qa_group()},
124	    'required': ['bloc_principal', 'questions_e', 'questions_f'],
125	    'additionalProperties': False,
126	}
127	_SCHEMA_NESTED_QA = {
128	    'type': 'object',
129	    'properties': {
130	        'bloc_principal': {'type': 'string'},
131	        'questions': {
132	            'type': 'object',
133	            'properties': {'questions_e': _qa_group(), 'questions_f': _qa_group()},
134	            'required': ['questions_e', 'questions_f'],

143	    'exec/pays_ville_exec.json': _SCHEMA_NESTED_QA,
144	    'exec/prompts_exec_profile_ville.json': _SCHEMA_FLAT_QA,
145	    'marche/prompts_type1_pays_marche.json': _SCHEMA_BLOC_ONLY,

151	# ---- question extraction: pin the E/F questions into the schema -----------
152	# Some prompts list their 10 questions explicitly ("❖ Question E1: ..."). When we
153	# can extract them RELIABLY we pin each one into the schema with `enum`, which
154	# makes a wrong/invented question impossible instead of merely discouraged.
155	# The extractor is deliberately strict: anything unexpected returns None and the
156	# caller falls back to the generic schema (fail safe, never pin garbage).
157	
158	_Q_LETTERED = re.compile(r'❖ Question\s*([EF])\s*(\d)\s*:\s*(.+)')
159	
160	# Files whose prompts use the lettered form. Verified over 100% of records:
161	#   prompts_exec_profile_ville.json -> 286,605/286,605 have exactly E1-E5, F1-F5
162	#   type3_pays_ville_presentation   ->     579/579     idem
163	LETTERED_FILES = {
164	    'exec/prompts_exec_profile_ville.json',
165	    'marche/prompts_type3_pays_ville_presentation.json',
166	}
167	
168	
169	def extract_questions_lettered(prompt):
170	    """Return {'E': [q1..q5], 'F': [q1..q5]} or None if anything is off.
171	
172	    NOTE: a plain '❖ Question:' regex would also match the 2 placeholder lines in
173	    the FORMAT block of these prompts — which is why we require the LETTER+DIGIT.
174	    """
175	    found = _Q_LETTERED.findall(prompt)
176	    if len(found) != 10:
177	        return None
178	    out = {'E': [None] * 5, 'F': [None] * 5}
179	    for cat, digit, text in found:
180	        i = int(digit)
181	        if not 1 <= i <= 5:
182	            return None
183	        if out[cat][i - 1] is not None:      # duplicate slot (e.g. two E3)
184	            return None
185	        text = text.strip()
186	        # a question must be real text, not a placeholder or a stray token
187	        if len(text) < 10 or text.lower().startswith('[') or text.lower() == 'string':
188	            return None
189	        # SQL-escape artifact in the source data ("M\'Sila", "Cote d\'Ivoire").
190	        # A backslash inside an `enum` value makes OpenAI's constrained decoder
191	        # truncate the string mid-word (verified: same request succeeds once the
192	        # backslash is removed), and it reports finish_reason=stop so the
193	        # truncation is silent. The backslash is not part of the real name, so
194	        # drop it before the text is ever used as an enum value.
195	        text = text.replace("\\'", "'")
196	        out[cat][i - 1] = text
197	    if any(v is None for v in out['E'] + out['F']):
198	        return None                          # a slot never filled -> incomplete
199	    return out
200

202	def questions_for(rel, prompt):
203	    """Extracted questions for this record, or None when pinning doesn't apply."""
204	    if str(rel).replace('\\', '/') in LETTERED_FILES:
205	        return extract_questions_lettered(prompt)
206	    return None

209	def _pinned_qa_group(questions):
210	    """questions_e/f block where each question_N is PINNED to one exact string.
211	
212	    `enum` with a single value + strict mode makes any other text impossible to
213	    emit, so the model cannot invent a question or copy one from the wrong list.
214	    Pinning question_N also anchors reponse_N, because generation is sequential.
215	    """
216	    props, req = {}, []
217	    for i in range(1, 6):
218	        props[f'question_{i}'] = {'type': 'string', 'enum': [questions[i - 1]]}
219	        props[f'reponse_{i}'] = {'type': 'string'}
220	        req += [f'question_{i}', f'reponse_{i}']
221	    return {'type': 'object', 'properties': props, 'required': req,
222	            'additionalProperties': False}
223

225	def _pinned_schema(shape, qs):
226	    """Build the file's schema with the 10 questions pinned. `shape` is 'flat'
227	    or 'nested', matching the file's FORMAT section."""
228	    e, f = _pinned_qa_group(qs['E']), _pinned_qa_group(qs['F'])
229	    if shape == 'nested':
230	        return {'type': 'object',
231	                'properties': {'bloc_principal': {'type': 'string'},
232	                               'questions': {'type': 'object',
233	                                             'properties': {'questions_e': e, 'questions_f': f},
234	                                             'required': ['questions_e', 'questions_f'],
235	                                             'additionalProperties': False}},
236	                'required': ['bloc_principal', 'questions'],
237	                'additionalProperties': False}
238	    return {'type': 'object',
239	            'properties': {'bloc_principal': {'type': 'string'},
240	                           'questions_e': e, 'questions_f': f},
241	            'required': ['bloc_principal', 'questions_e', 'questions_f'],
242	            'additionalProperties': False}

245	def response_format_for(rel, prompt=None):
246	    """Strict schema for a known file; plain json_object mode for unknown ones
247	    (still guarantees valid JSON, just not the exact key layout).
248	
249	    When `prompt` is given and its 10 E/F questions can be extracted reliably,
250	    the questions are PINNED into the schema (see _pinned_qa_group). Anything
251	    unexpected falls back to the generic schema below — never pin garbage.
252	    """
253	    key = str(rel).replace('\\', '/')
254	    if prompt is not None and key in LETTERED_FILES:
255	        qs = questions_for(key, prompt)
256	        if qs is not None:
257	            base = RESPONSE_SCHEMAS.get(key)
258	            shape = 'nested' if (base and 'questions' in base.get('properties', {})) else 'flat'
259	            return {'type': 'json_schema',
260	                    'json_schema': {'name': 'reponse', 'strict': True,
261	                                    'schema': _pinned_schema(shape, qs)}}
262	    schema = RESPONSE_SCHEMAS.get(str(rel).replace('\\', '/'))
263	    if schema is None:
264	        return {'type': 'json_object'}
265	    return {'type': 'json_schema',
266	            'json_schema': {'name': 'reponse', 'strict': True, 'schema': schema}}

297	# ---- (1) LOADER: stream first N records without loading the whole file ----
298	def stream_records(path: Path, limit: int):
299	    """Yield the first `limit` JSON objects from a top-level JSON array.
300	
301	    Reads the file in chunks and decodes one object at a time with
302	    json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode, so a 2.3 GB file never enters memory whole.
303	    """
304	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
305	    buf = ''
306	    started = False   # have we passed the opening '['
307	    yielded = 0
308	    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
309	        while yielded < limit:
310	            if not started:
311	                # find the opening bracket of the array
312	                while '[' not in buf:
313	                    chunk = f.read(65536)
314	                    if not chunk:
315	                        return
316	                    buf += chunk
317	                buf = buf[buf.index('[') + 1:]
318	                started = True
319	
320	            # strip leading whitespace / commas
321	            buf = buf.lstrip()
322	            while buf[:1] in (',',):
323	                buf = buf[1:].lstrip()
324	            if buf[:1] == ']':
325	                return  # end of array
326	
327	            # need more data?
328	            if not buf:
329	                chunk = f.read(65536)
330	                if not chunk:
331	                    return
332	                buf += chunk
333	                continue
334	
335	            try:
336	                obj, idx = decoder.raw_decode(buf)
337	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
338	                # object spans past the buffer; pull more bytes
339	                chunk = f.read(65536)
340	                if not chunk:
341	                    return
342	                buf += chunk
343	                continue
344	
345	            buf = buf[idx:]
346	            yield obj
347	            yielded += 1
348

350	def stream_from(path: Path, start_offset: int, limit: int):
351	    """Yield (record, offset_after) starting at a byte offset inside the array.
352	
353	    offset_after is the absolute byte position just past the record, so it can be
354	    stored in the ledger and used to resume the next chunk without rescanning the
355	    file from byte 0. start_offset == 0 means "start of file, find the '[' first".
356	    """
357	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
358	    yielded = 0
359	    # Binary reads + incremental UTF-8 decoding: text-mode tell() returns an
360	    # opaque cookie, not a byte count, so offsets must be tracked by hand.
361	    utf8 = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
362	    buf = ''
363	    base = start_offset          # absolute byte offset of buf[0]
364	
365	    def consume(n):
366	        """Drop n chars off the front of buf, advancing `base` by their byte length."""
367	        nonlocal buf, base
368	        base += len(buf[:n].encode('utf-8'))
369	        buf = buf[n:]
370	
371	    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
372	        f.seek(start_offset)
373	        started = start_offset > 0
374	        while yielded < limit:
375	            if not started:
376	                while '[' not in buf:
377	                    raw = f.read(65536)
378	                    if not raw:
379	                        return
380	                    buf += utf8.decode(raw)
381	                consume(buf.index('[') + 1)
382	                started = True
383	
384	            consume(len(buf) - len(buf.lstrip()))
385	            while buf[:1] == ',':
386	                consume(1)
387	                consume(len(buf) - len(buf.lstrip()))
388	            if buf[:1] == ']':
389	                return
390	
391	            if not buf:
392	                raw = f.read(65536)
393	                if not raw:
394	                    return
395	                buf += utf8.decode(raw)
396	                continue
397	
398	            try:
399	                obj, idx = decoder.raw_decode(buf)
400	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
401	                raw = f.read(65536)
402	                if not raw:
403	                    return
404	                buf += utf8.decode(raw)
405	                continue
406	
407	            consume(idx)
408	            yield obj, base          # absolute byte position just past this record
409	            yielded += 1
410

524	def wait_and_download(client, batch_id, run_name, interval):
525	    print(f"\nwaiting on batch {batch_id} (every {interval}s)...")
526	    start = time.time()
527	    while True:
528	        batch = client.batches.retrieve(batch_id)
529	        rc = batch.request_counts
530	        el = time.time() - start
531	        print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {batch.status} | "
532	              f"{rc.completed}/{rc.total} (failed {rc.failed}) | "
533	              f"{int(el//60)}m {int(el%60)}s")
534	        if batch.status == "completed":
535	            break
536	        if batch.status in ("failed", "expired", "cancelled"):
537	            print(f"BATCH {batch.status.upper()}: {batch.errors}")
538	            return None
539	        time.sleep(interval)
540	
541	    content = client.files.content(batch.output_file_id)
542	    text = content.content.decode('utf-8')
543	    results_path = BATCH_DIR / f"results_{run_name}.jsonl"

610	# ---- CHUNK BUILDER: sizes itself against the Batch API limits ------------
611	def build_chunk(rel, slug, start_index, start_offset, want, model):
612	    """Build up to `want` requests starting at start_offset.
613	
614	    Stops early if the chunk would exceed MAX_BATCH_REQUESTS or MAX_BATCH_BYTES,
615	    so the caller never has to think about OpenAI's limits.
616	    Returns (requests, sidecar, offset_after, n_read).
617	    """
618	    path = BASE_DIR / rel
619	    cap = min(want, MAX_BATCH_REQUESTS)
620	    requests, sidecar = [], {}
621	    nbytes = 0
622	    ntokens = 0
623	    offset_after = start_offset
624	    n_read = 0
625	
626	    for record, off in stream_from(path, start_offset, cap):
627	        i = start_index + n_read
628	        n_read += 1
629	        offset_after = off
630	        prompt = record.get('prompt')
631	        if not prompt:
632	            continue
633	        custom_id = f"{slug}__{i}"
634	        req = {
635	            "custom_id": custom_id,
636	            "method": "POST",
637	            "url": "/v1/chat/completions",
638	            "body": {
639	                "model": model,
640	                "messages": [
641	                    {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
642	                    {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
643	                ],
644	                "max_completion_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
645	                "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
646	                "top_p": TOP_P,
647	                "seed": SEED,
648	                "response_format": response_format_for(rel, prompt),
649	            },
650	        }
651	        line_bytes = len(json.dumps(req, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')) + 1
652	        if requests and nbytes + line_bytes > MAX_BATCH_BYTES:
653	            n_read -= 1           # this record rolls into the next chunk
654	            offset_after = start_offset if n_read == 0 else prev_off
655	            break
656	        nbytes += line_bytes
657	        ntokens += count_tokens(SYSTEM_PROMPT) + count_tokens(prompt)
658	        requests.append(req)
659	        sidecar[custom_id] = record
660	        prev_off = off
661	
662	    return requests, sidecar, offset_after, n_read, nbytes, ntokens

665	def merge_append(results_text, sidecar, out_path):
666	    """Append merged records to the output file. Output grows chunk by chunk.
667	
668	    Returns a stats dict describing what came back, so the caller can log exactly
669	    what OpenAI returned rather than just a count.
670	    """
671	    responses = {}
672	    errors = []           # (custom_id, code, message) for anything not merged
673	    usage = {'prompt_tokens': 0, 'completion_tokens': 0}
674	    finish = {}           # finish_reason -> count ('length' means truncated output
675	    lengths = []          # response character counts
676	
677	    for line in results_text.strip().split('\n'):
678	        if not line:
679	            continue
680	        r = json.loads(line)
681	        cid = r.get('custom_id')
682	        resp = r.get('response') or {}
683	        if resp.get('status_code') == 200:
684	            try:
685	                ch0 = resp['body']['choices'][0]
686	                responses[cid] = ch0['message']['content']
687	                fr = ch0.get('finish_reason', '?')
688	                finish[fr] = finish.get(fr, 0) + 1
689	                lengths.append(len(responses[cid] or ''))
690	                u = resp['body'].get('usage') or {}
691	                usage['prompt_tokens'] += u.get('prompt_tokens', 0)
692	                usage['completion_tokens'] += u.get('completion_tokens', 0)
693	            except (KeyError, IndexError) as e:
694	                errors.append((cid, 'malformed_response', str(e)))
695	        else:
696	            err = (resp.get('body') or {}).get('error') or {}
697	            errors.append((cid, err.get('code') or f"http_{resp.get('status_code')}",
698	                           err.get('message', '')))
699	
700	    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
701	    written = 0
702	    with open(out_path, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:   # append, never truncate
703	        for cid, record in sidecar.items():
704	            if cid not in responses:
705	                continue
706	            merged = {}
707	            for k, v in record.items():
708	                if k == 'prompt':
709	                    merged['response'] = responses[cid]
710	                else:
711	                    merged[k] = v
712	            if 'response' not in merged:
713	                merged['response'] = responses[cid]
714	            f.write(json.dumps(merged, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')
715	            written += 1
716	
717	    # Records in the batch that produced neither a response nor an error line.
718	    missing = [c for c in sidecar if c not in responses
719	               and c not in {e[0] for e in errors}]
720	    return {
721	        'written': written, 'failed': len(errors), 'errors': errors,
722	        'usage': usage, 'finish': finish, 'missing': missing,
723	        'avg_chars': int(sum(lengths) / len(lengths)) if lengths else 0,
724	        'min_chars': min(lengths) if lengths else 0,
725	        'max_chars': max(lengths) if lengths else 0,
726	    }

737	def find_batch_by_run_name(client, run_name, scan=500):
738	    """Ask OpenAI whether a batch tagged with this run_name already exists.
739	
740	    submit() stamps metadata={"run_name": ...} on every batch, so a chunk whose
741	    intent was recorded but whose ledger write never landed can be identified and
742	    adopted instead of resent. Returns the batch or None.
743	    """
744	    seen = 0
745	    after = None
746	    while seen < scan:
747	        page = client.batches.list(limit=100, after=after) if after else client.batches.list(limit=100)
748	        data = list(page.data)
749	        if not data:
750	            return None
751	        for b in data:
752	            meta = b.metadata or {}
753	            if meta.get('run_name') == run_name:
754	                return b
755	            seen += 1
756	        after = data[-1].id
757	        if not getattr(page, 'has_more', False):
758	            return None
759	    return None

763	def orchestrate(client, rel, target, chunk_size, model, interval, concurrency,
764	                token_budget=DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET):
765	    slug = file_slug(rel)
766	    led = load_ledger(slug, rel)
767	    out_path = _output_path_for(slug, {slug: rel})
768	
769	    print(f"\n=== ORCHESTRATE {rel} ===")
770	    print(f"  target {target} | {chunk_size}/batch | max {concurrency} alive | "
771	          f"token budget {token_budget/1e6:.1f}M enqueued")
772	    print(f"  already completed {led['completed']} | "
773	          f"resume at record {led['next_index']} (byte {led['byte_offset']})")
774	
775	    def collect(ch):
776	        """Download a finished batch, merge it, mark done — logging exactly what came back."""
777	        run_name = f"{slug}_{led['run_tag']}_c{ch['chunk']}"
778	        batch = client.batches.retrieve(ch['batch_id'])
779	        content = client.files.content(batch.output_file_id)
780	        text = content.content.decode('utf-8')
781	        results_path = BATCH_DIR / f"results_{run_name}.jsonl"
782	        results_path.write_text(text, encoding='utf-8')
783	        sidecar = json.loads((BATCH_DIR / f"sidecar_{run_name}.json").read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
784	
785	        # Remember where the output ends BEFORE appending. If we die mid-merge,
786	        # the ledger still says 'merging' and the next run rewinds the file to
787	        # this mark before retrying — otherwise those rows land twice.
788	        ch['out_offset'] = out_path.stat().st_size if out_path.exists() else 0
789	        ch['status'] = 'merging'
790	        save_ledger(led)
791	
792	        st = merge_append(text, sidecar, out_path)
793	        ch['status'] = 'done'
794	        led['completed'] += st['written']
795	        save_ledger(led)
796	
797	        rc = batch.request_counts
798	        secs = (batch.completed_at - batch.created_at) if (
799	            batch.completed_at and batch.created_at) else None
800	        u = st['usage']
801	        print(f"\n  [chunk {ch['chunk']}] RESULTS RECEIVED")
802	        print(f"    batch name : {run_name}")
803	        print(f"    batch id   : {batch.id}")
804	        print(f"    metadata   : {dict(batch.metadata or {})}")
805	        print(f"    endpoint   : {batch.endpoint} | model: {model} | window: {batch.completion_window}")
806	        print(f"    files      : in={batch.input_file_id} out={batch.output_file_id}"
807	              + (f" err={batch.error_file_id}" if batch.error_file_id else ""))
808	        print(f"    records    : {ch['start_index']}-{ch['start_index']+ch.get('n_read',0)-1} "
809	              f"({ch['count']} sent)")
810	        print(f"    counts     : {rc.completed} completed / {rc.total} total / {rc.failed} failed")
811	        if secs is not None:
812	            print(f"    duration   : {secs//60}m {secs%60}s")
813	        print(f"    tokens used: {u['prompt_tokens']:,} in + {u['completion_tokens']:,} out "
814	              f"= {u['prompt_tokens']+u['completion_tokens']:,}")
815	        print(f"    finish     : {st['finish'] or '-'}"
816	              + ("   <-- 'length' = output hit max_completion_tokens and was CUT OFF"
817	                 if st['finish'].get('length') else ""))
818	        print(f"    resp chars : avg {st['avg_chars']} (min {st['min_chars']}, max {st['max_chars']})")
819	        print(f"    merged     : {st['written']} -> {out_path.name}")
820	        if st['errors']:
821	            from collections import Counter
822	            print(f"    ERRORS     : {st['failed']} -> {dict(Counter(e[1] for e in st['errors']))}")
823	            for cid, code, msg in st['errors'][:3]:
824	                print(f"      - {cid}: {code}: {msg[:100]}")
825	        if st['missing']:
826	            print(f"    MISSING    : {len(st['missing'])} records returned nothing "
827	                  f"(e.g. {st['missing'][:3]})")
828	        print(f"    progress   : {led['completed']}/{target}")
829	
830	        log_event({
831	            'event': 'results_received', 'run_name': run_name, 'batch_id': batch.id,
832	            'metadata': dict(batch.metadata or {}), 'file': rel, 'chunk': ch['chunk'],
833	            'model': model, 'endpoint': batch.endpoint,
834	            'input_file_id': batch.input_file_id, 'output_file_id': batch.output_file_id,
835	            'error_file_id': batch.error_file_id,
836	            'start_index': ch['start_index'], 'n_read': ch.get('n_read'),
837	            'sent': ch['count'], 'completed': rc.completed, 'total': rc.total,
838	            'failed_requests': rc.failed, 'duration_s': secs,
839	            'created_at': batch.created_at, 'completed_at': batch.completed_at,
840	            'prompt_tokens': u['prompt_tokens'], 'completion_tokens': u['completion_tokens'],
841	            'finish_reasons': st['finish'], 'merged': st['written'],
842	            'avg_chars': st['avg_chars'], 'min_chars': st['min_chars'],
843	            'max_chars': st['max_chars'],
844	            'errors': [{'custom_id': c, 'code': k, 'message': m} for c, k, m in st['errors'][:20]],
845	            'missing': st['missing'][:20],
846	            'results_file': str(results_path), 'progress': led['completed'],
847	        })
848	        return True

850	    def send(ch):
851	        """Submit a chunk. Returns 'ok', 'empty', or 'token_limit' (retry later)."""
852	        run_name = f"{slug}_{led['run_tag']}_c{ch['chunk']}"
853	        requests, sidecar, off_after, n_read, nbytes, ntokens = build_chunk(
854	            rel, slug, ch['start_index'], ch['start_offset'], ch['want'], model)
855	        if not requests:
856	            ch['status'] = 'empty'
857	            save_ledger(led)
858	            return 'empty'
859	        BATCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
860	        (BATCH_DIR / f"sidecar_{run_name}.json").write_text(
861	            json.dumps(sidecar, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
862	        try:
863	            batch_id = submit(client, requests, run_name)
864	        except Exception as e:
865	            if 'token_limit_exceeded' in str(e) or 'enqueued' in str(e).lower():
866	                ch['status'] = 'pending_submit'   # untouched; retried when room frees
867	                save_ledger(led)
868	                return 'token_limit'
869	            raise
870	        ch.update(batch_id=batch_id, status='in_flight', count=len(requests),
871	                  offset_after=off_after, n_read=n_read, tokens=ntokens)
872	        # Only ever move the frontier forward: a retried old chunk must not drag
873	        # next_index backwards over records later chunks already covered.
874	        if ch['start_index'] + n_read > led['next_index']:
875	            led['next_index'] = ch['start_index'] + n_read
876	            led['byte_offset'] = off_after
877	        save_ledger(led)
878	        return 'ok'
879	
880	    # 0. RECOVER interrupted merges: rows may have been appended without the
881	    #    ledger recording it. Rewind the output to the pre-merge mark so the
882	    #    retry re-appends them exactly once instead of duplicating them.
883	    for ch in led['chunks']:
884	        if ch['status'] == 'merging':
885	            mark = ch.get('out_offset', 0)
886	            size = out_path.stat().st_size if out_path.exists() else 0
887	            if size > mark:
888	                with open(out_path, 'r+b') as f:
889	                    f.truncate(mark)
890	                print(f"\n-- chunk {ch['chunk']}: merge was interrupted. rewound output "
891	                      f"{size} -> {mark} bytes ({size-mark} bytes of partial/duplicate "
892	                      f"rows dropped), will re-merge")
893	            ch['status'] = 'in_flight'   # batch is still on OpenAI; collect it again
894	            save_ledger(led)
895	
896	    # 1. RECONCILE: settle every unfinished chunk against OpenAI before sending more.
897	    for ch in led['chunks']:
898	        if ch['status'] == 'pending_submit':
899	            # Crash happened around the create() call. Ask OpenAI what's true.
900	            run_name = f"{slug}_{led['run_tag']}_c{ch['chunk']}"
901	            print(f"\n-- chunk {ch['chunk']}: intent recorded but outcome unknown. "
902	                  f"asking OpenAI if it was already accepted...")
903	            b = find_batch_by_run_name(client, run_name)
904	            if b is not None and b.status not in ('failed', 'expired', 'cancelled'):
905	                print(f"  FOUND on OpenAI (batch {b.id}) — adopting it, not resending.")
906	                # The crash killed send() before it could advance the cursor, so
907	                # recompute this chunk's span (build_chunk is deterministic) and
908	                # move next_index past it — otherwise the next chunk restarts on
909	                # records this batch already covers and duplicates them.
910	                _r, _s, off_after, n_read, _b, _t = build_chunk(
911	                    rel, slug, ch['start_index'], ch['start_offset'], ch['want'], model)
912	                ch.update(batch_id=b.id, status='in_flight',
913	                          count=len(_r), offset_after=off_after, n_read=n_read, tokens=_t)
914	                if ch['start_index'] + n_read > led['next_index']:
915	                    led['next_index'] = ch['start_index'] + n_read
916	                    led['byte_offset'] = off_after
917	                save_ledger(led)
918	            else:
919	                print(f"  never landed on OpenAI — queued for retry.")
920	                ch['status'] = 'failed'    # picked up by the retry pass below
921	                save_ledger(led)
922	
923	    # Anything already in_flight simply rejoins the pool below — no resend.
924	    pool = [ch for ch in led['chunks'] if ch['status'] == 'in_flight']
925	    if pool:
926	        print(f"\n-- rejoining {len(pool)} batch(es) already in flight: "
927	              f"{[c['chunk'] for c in pool]}")
928	
929	    exhausted = False
930	
931	    def enqueued():
932	        return sum(c.get('tokens', 0) for c in pool)
933	
934	    def dispatch(ch, label):
935	        """Send an already-budgeted chunk. Returns 'ok'/'empty'/'token_limit'."""
936	        r = send(ch)
937	        if r == 'ok':
938	            pool.append(ch)
939	            run_name = f"{slug}_{led['run_tag']}_c{ch['chunk']}"
940	            print(f"  [chunk {ch['chunk']}] SENT{label}: {run_name} | batch {ch['batch_id']} | "
941	                  f"records {ch['start_index']}-{ch['start_index']+ch['n_read']-1} "
942	                  f"({ch['count']} reqs, ~{ch['tokens']/1000:.0f}k tok) | "
943	                  f"pool {len(pool)}/{concurrency}, enqueued ~{enqueued()/1e6:.2f}M/"
944	                  f"{token_budget/1e6:.1f}M")
945	            log_event({'event': 'sent', 'run_name': run_name, 'batch_id': ch['batch_id'],
946	                       'file': rel, 'chunk': ch['chunk'], 'model': model,
947	                       'start_index': ch['start_index'], 'n_read': ch['n_read'],
948	                       'requests': ch['count'], 'est_tokens': ch['tokens'],
949	                       'retry': bool(label.strip()), 'pool_size': len(pool),
950	                       'enqueued_tokens': enqueued()})
951	        elif r == 'token_limit':
952	            print(f"  [chunk {ch['chunk']}] enqueued-token limit hit — backing off, "
953	                  f"retrying when a batch completes")
954	        return r
955	
956	    def fill():
957	        """Top the pool back up, retrying failed chunks FIRST so no records are lost.
958	
959	        The token budget is checked BEFORE an intent is recorded: writing an intent
960	        we then decline to send would orphan it, and the next run's reconcile would
961	        resend records a later chunk had already covered.
962	        """
963	        nonlocal exhausted
964	        while len(pool) < concurrency:
965	            # 1. Retry a previously failed chunk before advancing the frontier.
966	            retry = next((c for c in led['chunks'] if c['status'] == 'failed'), None)
967	            if retry is not None:
968	                _r, _s, _o, _n, _b, est = build_chunk(
969	                    rel, slug, retry['start_index'], retry['start_offset'],
970	                    retry['want'], model)
971	                if pool and enqueued() + est > token_budget:
972	                    return
973	                if dispatch(retry, ' (retry)') != 'ok':
974	                    return
975	                continue
976	
977	            if exhausted or led['next_index'] >= target:
978	                return
979	
980	            # 2. New chunk: price it BEFORE recording intent.
981	            want = min(chunk_size, target - led['next_index'])
982	            probe, _s, _o, _n, _b, est = build_chunk(
983	                rel, slug, led['next_index'], led['byte_offset'], want, model)
984	            if not probe:
985	                exhausted = True
986	                print("  no more records in file.")
987	                return
988	            if pool and enqueued() + est > token_budget:
989	                return   # no intent written — nothing to orphan
990	
991	            # INTENT FIRST (now that it's budgeted): recorded before OpenAI is
992	            # called, so a crash during create() is resolved by asking OpenAI.
993	            ch = {"chunk": len(led['chunks']), "start_index": led['next_index'],
994	                  "start_offset": led['byte_offset'], "want": want,
995	                  "batch_id": None, "status": "pending_submit"}
996	            led['chunks'].append(ch)
997	            save_ledger(led)
998	            if dispatch(ch, '') != 'ok':
999	                return
1000	
1001	    # 2. Pool loop: keep the pool as full as the token budget allows; as each
1002	    #    batch lands, merge it and send a replacement, until target is consumed.
1003	    fill()
1004	    while pool:
1005	        time.sleep(interval)
1006	        for ch in list(pool):
1007	            b = client.batches.retrieve(ch['batch_id'])
1008	            rc_ = b.request_counts
1009	            ch['prog'] = (rc_.completed, rc_.total) if rc_ else (0, ch.get('count', 0))
1010	            if b.status == 'completed':
1011	                pool.remove(ch)
1012	                collect(ch)
1013	            elif b.status in ('failed', 'expired', 'cancelled'):
1014	                errs = []
1015	                try:
1016	                    d = b.errors.data if (b.errors and hasattr(b.errors, 'data')) else None
1017	                    errs = [{'code': getattr(e, 'code', None),
1018	                             'message': getattr(e, 'message', str(e))} for e in (d or [])]
1019	                except Exception:
1020	                    pass
1021	                run_name = f"{slug}_{led['run_tag']}_c{ch['chunk']}"
1022	                print(f"\n  [chunk {ch['chunk']}] {b.status.upper()}")
1023	                print(f"    batch name : {run_name}")
1024	                print(f"    batch id   : {b.id}")
1025	                print(f"    metadata   : {dict(b.metadata or {})}")
1026	                for e in errs[:3]:
1027	                    print(f"    reason     : {e['code']}: {e['message']}")
1028	                print(f"    -> records {ch['start_index']}-"
1029	                      f"{ch['start_index']+ch.get('n_read',0)-1} queued for retry")
1030	                log_event({'event': b.status, 'run_name': run_name, 'batch_id': b.id,
1031	                           'metadata': dict(b.metadata or {}), 'file': rel,
1032	                           'chunk': ch['chunk'], 'model': model,
1033	                           'start_index': ch['start_index'], 'n_read': ch.get('n_read'),
1034	                           'requests': ch.get('count'), 'errors': errs})
1035	                ch['status'] = 'failed'
1036	                ch['tokens'] = 0
1037	                save_ledger(led)
1038	                pool.remove(ch)
1039	        fill()   # refill the moment slots (and tokens) free up
1040	        if pool:
1041	            rc = [f"c{c['chunk']}({c['prog'][0]}/{c['prog'][1]})" if c.get('prog')
1042	                  else f"c{c['chunk']}" for c in pool]
1043	            print(f"  ... {led['completed']}/{target} done | {len(pool)} alive: {' '.join(rc)}")
1044	
1045	    print(f"\n=== {rel}: {led['completed']} records done -> {out_path} ===")

1093	            done = sum(1 for c in led['chunks'] if c['status'] == 'done')

1096	            print(f"{rel}: {led['completed']} completed | next record {led['next_index']} | "
